clue.text: Swimming group turned aquatic vehicle into something for children to ride on

definitions.text: something for children to ride on

parts.note: a school is a large group of fish swimming together

indicators.note: turned means the word for the vessel is flipped end to end

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, travels underwater

explanation.surface: Something about a swimming club and a submarine being converted into a children's ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Children are carried to their lessons on this vehicle, so it is something they ride on daily.

clue.text: Small fish is upset

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A little fish has been disturbed or is out of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to unsettle or rattle them, which is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Dangerous weapon used by female in docked part of ship

indicators.note: in places the weapon and the female abbreviation inside the trimmed ship part
docked means cut short, as a tail is, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the hull is the main body of a ship
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A woman wields a weapon in the hold of a moored ship, which sounds dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' suggests a ship in harbour, but it means cutting the last letter off HULL to give HUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangerous is likely to cause damage or injury, the same sense as the adjective.

clue.text: Obstreperous Russian initially rejected communist's directive

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it
rejected means turned back, so the colour word for a communist is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist; the 's here is just possessive dressing

explanation.surface: A rowdy Russian refused to obey a Communist Party instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A directive is an instruction from authority, a synonym of a command or mandate.

clue.text: Man obtaining image used by the police has an advantage

parts.note: Ben is a man's name, short for Benjamin
an E-FIT is a computer-generated likeness of a suspect built from witness descriptions, used by British police

explanation.surface: A man who is caught on a police composite picture is somehow better off.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or advantage, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Unstable suspect cornering Republican soldier

indicators.note: cornering means hemming in, so the rearranged letters surround the party letter
suspect means dubious or questionable, signalling the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican, as in US politics

explanation.surface: A shaky suspect has a Republican trapped in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun, but it is the anagram signal working on UNSTABLE, which makes SUBALTEN; R goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a junior army officer below captain, so a soldier by rank.

clue.text: Clothing for cold animal

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
an ape is an animal, such as a gorilla

explanation.surface: A garment designed for an animal in chilly weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a sleeveless cloak, an example of clothing.

clue.text: Invents a story about spook wandering round university

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the university letter
wandering means roaming about, signalling the letters move out of order

explanation.surface: Someone makes up a tale of a ghost roaming around a university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook up a tale is an idiom for fabricating or concocting it.

clue.text: Sum of money gets space at gallery for person of influence

parts.note: a pot is a sum of money, as in a jackpot or kitty
an en is a printer's unit of space
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A cash pot buys some room at an art gallery for a VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or ruler, someone wielding great power and influence.

clue.text: Domineering woman and son dropping off type of tweed with short Scandinavian

indicators.note: dropping off means the son letter falls away from the fabric name

parts.note: Harris tweed is a cloth woven in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the nationality word

parts.note: a Dane is a person from Denmark, in Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A bossy woman and her son nod off beside some tweed and a short Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' sounds like falling asleep; it means losing S from HARRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, belligerent old woman, close to a synonym for a domineering one.

clue.text: Blonde heading to bingo is drunk

indicators.note: heading means the front, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: lotto is a game like bingo, with numbers called and cards marked

explanation.surface: A blonde woman goes off to the bingo hall thoroughly inebriated.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely intoxicated.

clue.text: Soldiers free to relax with spliff

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: to relax means to loosen, so the letters are slackened into a new order

explanation.surface: Off-duty soldiers are free to unwind with a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a cannabis cigarette, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Fellow looks afresh at New Guinea's traditional music

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

indicators.note: afresh means anew, so these letters are arranged again

parts.note: NG is the abbreviation for New Guinea

explanation.surface: A man takes a new look at the music of New Guinea.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk song is a traditional tune handed down orally, so an example of traditional music.

clue.text: Beggar licensed to carry vegetable

indicators.note: to carry means the two words hold the answer within them across the join

explanation.surface: A street beggar has been given a licence to bear some vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic is a bulb of the onion family, grown and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Cargo unit dispatched to old European battle

indicators.note: dispatched means sent off, and here the letters are sent into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A freight container is shipped off to the scene of a historic battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt in 1415 was a famous English victory over the French, a battle of medieval Europe.

clue.text: Immobile jazz fan given a shot in the arm

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a tonic is a boost or pick-me-up, figuratively a shot in the arm

explanation.surface: A jazz lover lies motionless after an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot in the arm' reads as an injection, but it is the idiom for a revitalising boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic person is in a rigid stupor, so unmoving or immobile.

clue.text: Neat ship designed by arty type

indicators.note: designed means planned out, so the letters are arranged into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A smart vessel was drawn up by a creative person.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, someone from the arts world, hence an arty type.

clue.text: Awful chapter given to graduate's second supervisor

parts.note: dire means dreadful or awful

indicators.note: second picks out the letter in position two of the word

explanation.surface: A terrible chapter is handed to a graduate's second supervisor for review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second supervisor' reads as a thesis examiner, but 'second' takes letter two of 'graduate's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A director oversees and manages work, so is a supervisor in the general sense.

clue.text: 10 tucked into extremely expensive and charming produce

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the numeral sits between the two end letters
extremely takes the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
cute means attractive or charming

explanation.surface: Ten items squeezed into an expensive and delightful product range.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10-across, but it is simply the Roman numeral X.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce a plan or a work is to carry it out, the sense of executing it.

clue.text: Animal artist joining company involved in swindle

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the company abbreviation goes within the swindle word

parts.note: a con is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: An animal painter teams up with a firm caught up in a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: The raccoon is a North American mammal with a masked face, an example of an animal.

clue.text: New priest leaving fruit in Italian city

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the priest letter is removed from the fruit word

parts.note: apples are a fruit

explanation.surface: A newly ordained priest leaves some fruit behind in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a major port city in southern Italy, an example of an Italian city.

clue.text: Large sniper drunk lager

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A big sharpshooter downs a pint of lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the verb from the drinking scene, but it is the anagram signal on L plus SNIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilsner is a pale, hoppy lager first brewed in Pilsen, so an example of lager.

clue.text: European clergyman dropping king in favour of court is catholic

indicators.note: dropping means the king's letter is removed from the churchman word
in favour of means the court abbreviation is put in the place freed up

parts.note: a cleric is a member of the clergy
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A churchman from Europe abandons the monarch and sides with the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' with a small c means wide-ranging, not the church, despite the clergyman in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowercase catholic means broad and all-embracing in taste, which matches eclectic, drawing from many sources.

clue.text: Choose to promote short and shocking treatment

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to sell a product is to promote it
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, an electric-shock treatment

explanation.surface: Choosing to advertise a brief, shocking course of therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to pick out from options, a direct synonym of choose.

clue.text: Inflexible part of ship?

definitions.meaning: strict and unbending in manner or attitude
the rear section of a vessel, opposite the bow

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both severe and unyielding and the back end of a boat.

clue.text: Elite clubs given pieces of paper

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
a ream is a quantity of paper sheets, traditionally 480 or 500

explanation.surface: Exclusive clubs are handed some bits of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best part, the elite, as cream rises to the top.

clue.text: Reddish-coloured gold found next to Scottish stream

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
burn is the Scottish word for a small stream

explanation.surface: Reddish gold is discovered beside a Highland brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown shade, usually of hair.

clue.text: Old person putting up the money to conserve a plant

indicators.note: to conserve means to keep safe within, so the lender holds the letter A inside

parts.note: a lender advances money to a borrower

explanation.surface: An elderly financier backs a plan to conserve a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen shrub with showy flowers, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Rhinoplasty effectively conceals swelling

indicators.note: conceals means the two words keep the answer tucked inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: A nose job does a good job of hiding a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the edge of the eyelid.

clue.text: Pretend to welcome woman with drink problem

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so the fake word receives the woman inside it

parts.note: cod, in British usage, means fake or mock, as in cod philosophy
a nun is a religious woman
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone feigns a warm greeting to a woman who has a drinking problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink problem' reads as one phrase, but 'problem' is the definition; COD is British for sham.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling or difficult question, a synonym for problem.
